name: Sakura Garden
description: Sakura Garden offers an authentic Japanese fine dining experience in the heart of Tokyo. Our expert chefs craft each dish with seasonal ingredients sourced from the finest local markets. From delicate sashimi platters to expertly prepared wagyu beef, every plate is a work of art. Our intimate setting, adorned with traditional ikebana floral arrangements and soft paper lanterns, creates a serene escape from the bustling city.
shortDescription: Authentic Japanese fine dining with seasonal omakase menus in the heart of Tokyo.

name: The Spice Route
description: The Spice Route is a vibrant celebration of India's rich culinary heritage. From the smoky aromas of our tandoor oven to the fragrant curries simmering with hand-ground spices, every meal is a journey across the subcontinent. Our menu features regional specialties from Punjab, Kerala, Rajasthan, and Bengal, ensuring a diverse and immersive dining experience. Pair your meal with a chilled mango lassi or a fine selection from our chai bar.
shortDescription: A vibrant journey through India's regional cuisines with authentic spices and tandoor specialties.

name: La Bella Italia
description: La Bella Italia is a classic Milanese trattoria where tradition meets modern flair. Our pasta is hand-rolled daily using recipes passed down through three generations of the Ferrari family. The wood-fired pizza oven, imported directly from Naples, ensures an authentically crispy crust with every pie. With an extensive cellar of Italian wines from Tuscany, Piedmont, and Sicily, La Bella Italia is the perfect setting for a romantic dinner or a festive family gathering.
shortDescription: Generations-old family trattoria serving hand-rolled pasta and wood-fired pizza with an Italian wine cellar.

name: Golden Dragon Palace
description: Golden Dragon Palace brings the grandeur of imperial Shanghai to your table. Our dim sum carts roll through the dining hall all day, while the chefs hand-pull noodles and carve Peking duck tableside. Steamed buns, chili crab, and wok-fired greens share the menu with a curated selection of fine teas served in traditional gaiwan.
shortDescription: Imperial-style Chinese dining with all-day dim sum carts and tableside Peking duck.

name: Bangkok Basil Kitchen
description: Bangkok Basil Kitchen serves the bold, punchy flavours of a Bangkok soi in a sleek, breezy setting. Green curry with fresh basil, charcoal-grilled satay, som tam, and a signature seafood tom yum come straight from recipes perfected on the streets of Old Town. Spice levels are honest — ask for the good stuff.
shortDescription: Street-style Thai food with bold flavours, from green curry to flame-grilled satay.

name: Le Petit Bistro
description: A gravel-voiced bistro on the Left Bank, Le Petit Bistro does classic French cooking with zero fuss. Steak frites, duck confit, a properly glossy ris de veau, and cheese from the morning market. The wine list tips heavily to Burgundy and the Loire, all served with crusty baguette and better conversation.
shortDescription: Classic Parisian bistro — steak frites, duck confit, and a Burgundy-heavy wine wall.

name: Casa Veracruz
address: Av. Álvaro Obregón 199, Roma Norte, CDMX 06700
description: Casa Veracruz punches in from the Gulf coast: cocteles de camarón, octopus ceviche, and fish tacos on house-made tortillas. The agave bar is stocked with 200+ mezcales, and weekend brunch pairs huevos rancheros with live son jarocho. Loud, colourful, and always packed.
shortDescription: Coastal Mexican seafood and an enormous mezcal library in the heart of Roma Norte.

name: Olive & Sea Taverna
description: Under a grapevine canopy in the Plaka, Olive & Sea Taverna grills whole fish over charcoal and dresses it simply with tzatziki, lemon, and good oil. Meze plates — tirokafteri, grilled octopus, gigantes beans — arrive like a parade. The Retsina flows, the plates never stop.
shortDescription: Charcoal-grilled fish and endless meze under the grapevines of Plaka.

name: Seoul Fire Table
description: Seoul Fire Table is built around an in-table charcoal grill where marinated pork belly and wagyu short rib singe over hardwood. Every table gets a battalion of banchan — kimchi, pickled radish, seasoned spinach — refreshed without asking. Finish with sizzling bibimbap in a stone pot and cold soju.
shortDescription: Tabletop charcoal Korean BBQ with an endless changing carousel of banchan.

name: Saigon Lantern
description: Saigon Lantern simmers its pho broth for eighteen hours, then lets you season it your way — lime, bird's eye chilli, raw herb mountain. Beyond the noodle bowl, the menu runs through fresh rice-paper rolls, sizzling bánh xèo, and a bánh mì that justifies a queue. Bright, fast, and deeply fragrant.
shortDescription: Eighteen-hour pho broth, fresh rice-paper rolls, and bánh mì worth queueing for.

name: Smoky Ember Steakhouse
address: 445 N Dearborn St, River North, Chicago IL 60654
description: Smoky Ember dry-ages its beef for 45 days then throws it over oak and hickory. The ribeye is the headline, but the smoked short rib, bone marrow gratin, and whiskey program keep regulars loyal. Big booths, dim light, a chalkboard of cuts, and steak knives that mean business.
shortDescription: 45-day dry-aged beef over oak, a serious whiskey wall, and a chalkboard of cuts.

name: Sugar & Spice Café
description: A sun-drenched café in Ubud where coffee is roasted on site and desserts lean tropical — coconut pandan waffles, dragonfruit cheesecake, and molten brownies with kaffir lime. Brunch runs until late afternoon; the avocado toast and cold brew are the gateways. Dogs welcome, laptops tolerated before noon.
shortDescription: Tropical café for lazy brunches — on-site roasted coffee and pandan-coconut desserts.

name: Nori Bay Sushi
description: Nori Bay Sushi is a nine-seat counter where edomae nigiri arrives at the right temperature and the right pace. The rice is seasoned with red vinegar; hokkaido uni, toro, and cuttlefish rotate with the morning catch from Osaka Bay. No menu, no pictures — just trust the counter.
shortDescription: Nine-seat edomae counter serving omakase nigiri from the morning catch.

name: Tandoor Tales
description: Tandoor Tales tells Delhi's story through fire. Seekh kebabs and garam masala chicken leave the clay oven blistered and smoky, mopped up with garlic naan that arrives torn apart and butter-brushed. The butter chicken is the classic's benchmark; the lassi counter handles the rest.
shortDescription: Clay-oven kebabs and a benchmark butter chicken in the heart of Khan Market.

name: Nonna's Wine Kitchen
description: Nonna's Wine Kitchen cooks like a Sunday in a Tuscan farmhouse — ribollita thick as porridge, pappardelle with wild boar ragù, pecorino straight from the mountainside. The wine list reads like a walking tour of Chianti. Cash is happy, reservation is better.
shortDescription: Sunday-in-Tuscany cooking — wild boar ragù, ribollita, and a Chianti-centric cellar.

name: Szechuan Fire Wok
description: Szechuan Fire Wok treats mala heat as a language. Mapo tofu leaves your lips numb and smiling, whole dry-chilli fish lands like a fireworks display, and the hot pot lets you chart your own spice course. Cold beers and cucumber salads are the circuit breakers.
shortDescription: Numbing, mouth-firing Szechuan classics and build-your-own-spice hot pot.

name: Chao Phraya House
address: 108 Charoen Rat Rd, Wat Ket, Chiang Mai 50000
description: Along the Mae Ping river, Chao Phraya House does the slow-cooked flavours of Northern Thailand. Khao soi with crackly noodles, larb gai sharp with toasted rice powder, and a jungle curry that doesn't apologise. Dinner service is unhurried, candle-lit, and accompanied by a jazz record or two.
shortDescription: Riverside Northern Thai kitchen — khao soi, larb, and unhurried jungle curries.

name: Maison Lumière
description: Maison Lumière is a proper Lyonnais bouchon: checkered cloths, glass of beaujolais, and a quenelle so light it almost floats. The menu runs the classic line — cervelle de canut, pike quenelle, andouillette for the brave. Friendly, generous, and gloriously unpretentious.
shortDescription: Lyon's classic bouchon — featherlight pike quenelles and honest beaujolais.

name: Dos Hermanos Cantina
address: Av. Chapultepec Sur 68, Col Americana, 44160 GDL
description: Dos Hermanos Cantina is a Jalisco taquería at heart: birria de res ladled into consommé, tortas ahogadas that demand a bib, and tacos al pastor carved straight off the trompo. The margarita list is long and the mariachi starts Thursday. Come hungry, leave loud.
shortDescription: Guadalajara-style birria, trompo al pastor, and a margarita list as long as the night.

name: Levante Kitchen
address: Carrer del Parlament 28, El Poble-sec, 08015 Barcelona
description: Levante Kitchen rides the Mediterranean coast from Cádiz to Valencia. Jamón carved to order, gambas al ajillo sizzling in clay, and a paella cooked over olive wood on busy Sundays. The vermouth comes on tap and the counter seats face the open fire.
shortDescription: Coast-to-coast Spanish: jamón, sizzling gambas, and olive-wood Sunday paella.

name: Gangnam Grill House
description: Overlooking Haeundae beach, Gangnam Grill House pairs thick-cut pork belly with the day's seafood from the nearby Jagalchi market. Tables grill over real charcoal while makgeolli is served in brass bowls. The view, the smoke, and the soundtrack of sizzling fat make it a scene.
shortDescription: Beachfront charcoal grill — pork belly, Busan seafood, and makgeolli in brass bowls.

name: Mekong Delta Eatery
address: 27 P. Lương Văn Can, Hoàn Kiếm, Hanoi 100000
description: Mekong Delta Eatery is a love letter to the river's kitchen. Bánh xèo crackles in the pan, snails arrive in a lemongrass broth, and every platter is a wall of herbs and rice paper waiting to be assembled by hand. Fast, fragrant, and stubbornly authentic.
shortDescription: The Delta on a plate — crisp bánh xèo, lemongrass snails, and DIY rice-paper rolls.

name: Argentinian Asado Club
address: Juana Manso 1640, Puerto Madero, C1107 CABA
description: Argentinian Asado Club grills over glowing embers in Puerto Madero. Bife de chorizo, sweetbreads, and long-cooked ribs arrive on a board with chimichurri that deserves its own religion. Malbec by the magnum, a discada of criollos, and the smell of smoke that follows you out.
shortDescription: Ember-grilled asado in Puerto Madero — bife de chorizo, sweetbreads, and Malbec by the magnum.

name: Bloom Bakery & Brunch
description: Bloom Bakery & Brunch fills a canal-side corner with the smell of croissant laminating and fresh espresso. Shokupan breakfast sandwiches, seasonal tarts, and a pastry case that empties before noon. The open kitchen lets you watch the bakers at work; the queue is part of the charm.
shortDescription: Canalside bakery and brunch — laminated croissants, shokupan sandwiches, and seasonal tarts.

name: Ichiban Ramen Bar
description: Ichiban Ramen Bar is a twelve-stool ramen counter where the tonkotsu broth simmers for two days. Chashu is braised until it shivers, ajitama eggs are marinated overnight, and the extra-rich tsukemen demands a stretch after. Slurp loudly — it's a compliment here.
shortDescription: Twelve-stool ramen counter with two-day tonkotsu broth and overnight-marinated eggs.

name: Curry Leaf Junction
description: Curry Leaf Junction celebrates the south: dosa that crackles like thunder, Meen curry with coconut and curry leaf, and appam so light they could be mistaken for dreams. The banana-leaf thali is the full tour and the filter coffee hits like a small wake-up call.
shortDescription: South Indian ode — thunder-crackle dosa, coconut fish curry, and the full banana-leaf thali.

name: Vino & Pasta Cucina
address: Via del Governo Vecchio 102, 00186 Roma RM
description: Vino & Pasta Cucina is a Roman trattoria that does the six pasta dishes Rome actually argues about — cacio e pepe, carbonara with guanciale, amatriciana. The bucatini is ladled out at a worn marble counter and the house vino della casa comes by the quartino. No substitutions, no regrets.
shortDescription: Rome's argumentative six — cacio e pepe, carbonara, and amatriciana at a marble counter.
